calderetang-manok.name: Calderetang Manok
calderetang-manok.notes: Simmer browned chicken and aromatics in tomato sauce and water, then cook vegetables until tender and stir in liver spread. Adaptations: skinless boneless breast replaces chicken parts; 56 g weighed liver spread replaces the source's unweighed spoon quantity. Cheese and bouillon are omitted. Quantities are measured inputs for the listed batch, divided by its serving count. Cooked weight and evaporation are not measured. Extra salt, oil and garnishes are excluded unless listed.

calderetang-baka.name: Calderetang Baka
calderetang-baka.notes: Braise beef until tender before adding vegetables and thickening with liver spread. Adaptations: trimmed lean chuck; water replaces broth; two 56 g Palm label servings replace the unweighed half-cup of spread. Olives and extra salt omitted. Counted produce uses the documented USDA reference size. Quantities are ingredient inputs for the listed batch, divided by its serving count. Cooked weight and evaporation are not measured. Extra salt, oil and garnishes are excluded unless listed; record measured additions when used.

menudo.name: Menudo
menudo.notes: Marinate pork with citrus and soy sauce. Saute aromatics and pork, simmer with tomato sauce and water, then cook potatoes, carrot and liver through. Adaptations: trimmed shoulder; optional hotdogs and extra salt omitted. Counted produce uses the documented USDA reference size. Quantities are ingredient inputs for the listed batch, divided by its serving count. Cooked weight and evaporation are not measured. Extra salt, oil and garnishes are excluded unless listed; record measured additions when used.

adobong-manok.name: Adobong Manok
adobong-manok.notes: Saute chicken, onion and garlic, add soy sauce and vinegar, then simmer until cooked. Broil the chicken and reduce the sauce separately. Adaptations: one measured teaspoon of canola oil replaces olive oil; paprika, the source pepper amount and optional garnish are omitted. Quantities are measured inputs for the listed batch, divided by its serving count. Cooked weight and evaporation are not measured. Extra salt, oil and garnishes are excluded unless listed.

adobong-baboy.name: Adobong Baboy
adobong-baboy.notes: Simmer pork with garlic, vinegar, soy sauce, bay leaves and pepper until tender. Retains the source pork-belly preparation; no extra salt added. Counted produce uses the documented USDA reference size. Quantities are ingredient inputs for the listed batch, divided by its serving count. Cooked weight and evaporation are not measured. Extra salt, oil and garnishes are excluded unless listed; record measured additions when used.

asadong-manok.name: Asadong Manok
asadong-manok.notes: Marinate chicken, brown it and braise in the citrus-tomato sauce; cook potatoes separately and add at serving. Adaptations: skinless breast and fresh lemon juice; 28 g weighed Palm spread replaces the unweighed two tablespoons. Source oil is included in full; discarded frying oil is not measured. Counted produce uses the documented USDA reference size. Quantities are ingredient inputs for the listed batch, divided by its serving count. Cooked weight and evaporation are not measured. Extra salt, oil and garnishes are excluded unless listed; record measured additions when used.

paksiw-na-bangus.name: Paksiw na Bangus
paksiw-na-bangus.notes: Simmer fish and vegetables gently in vinegar and water until cooked. Whole-fish counts are replaced with four weighed 85 g edible portions; bones and trimming waste are excluded. Adaptations: measured ginger; optional whole chili omitted. Counted produce uses the documented USDA reference size. Quantities are ingredient inputs for the listed batch, divided by its serving count. Cooked weight and evaporation are not measured. Extra salt, oil and garnishes are excluded unless listed; record measured additions when used.

ginataang-tilapia.name: Ginataang Tilapia
ginataang-tilapia.notes: Saute aromatics, add coconut milk and simmer the fish until cooked. Add pechay near the end. Adaptations: two USDA-measured 116 g fillets replace whole fish; fresh fish is used without pre-frying; measured ginger and optional chilies omitted. Counted produce uses the documented USDA reference size. Quantities are ingredient inputs for the listed batch, divided by its serving count. Cooked weight and evaporation are not measured. Extra salt, oil and garnishes are excluded unless listed; record measured additions when used.

ginataang-kalabasa-at-sitaw.name: Ginataang Kalabasa at Sitaw
ginataang-kalabasa-at-sitaw.notes: Brown pork and saute aromatics, then simmer squash and sitaw in coconut milk. Eighteen yardlong-bean pods use the USDA reference weight of 12 g each. Adaptations: butternut squash and lean pork are the measured source foods; bouillon and unquantified fish sauce are omitted. Quantities are measured inputs for the listed batch, divided by its serving count. Cooked weight and evaporation are not measured. Extra salt, oil and garnishes are excluded unless listed.

tortang-talong.name: Tortang Talong
tortang-talong.notes: Boil the weighed eggplant until tender, flatten, coat with beaten egg and pan-cook in the measured oil. Adaptation: one 50 g chicken egg replaces the source 70 g duck egg. Use the source oil weight of 5 g; its printed drop count is not used. Unweighed seasoning is excluded. Counted produce uses the documented USDA reference size. Quantities are ingredient inputs for the listed batch, divided by its serving count. Cooked weight and evaporation are not measured. Extra salt, oil and garnishes are excluded unless listed; record measured additions when used.

suam-na-mais.name: Suam na Mais
suam-na-mais.notes: Cut kernels from the cobs and scrape their pulp. Saute aromatics, shrimp and bagoong, simmer with corn and water, then wilt the spinach. Adaptation: USDA sweet white corn replaces native glutinous corn; texture can differ. Bagoong is the named Barrio Fiesta product. Counted produce uses the documented USDA reference size. Quantities are ingredient inputs for the listed batch, divided by its serving count. Cooked weight and evaporation are not measured. Extra salt, oil and garnishes are excluded unless listed; record measured additions when used.

bulanglang-na-bangus-at-hipon.name: Bulanglang na Bangus at Hipon
bulanglang-na-bangus-at-hipon.notes: Simmer guava and onion, strain the guava seeds, then cook fish and shrimp gently and add kangkong. Uses 340 g weighed edible bangus and 340 g weighed kangkong in place of unweighed whole-fish and bunch counts. Guava nutrients count the edible input; straining losses are not measured. Quantities are inputs for four portions; cooked weight and evaporation are not measured.

bringhe.name: Bringhe
bringhe.notes: Saute chicken and aromatics, add rice, coconut milk, water and turmeric, then cook covered with vegetables and raisins until the rice is done. Garnish with the listed eggs. Adaptations: skinless breast replaces thigh; chorizo is omitted; water is the source alternative to broth. Quantities are measured inputs for the listed batch, divided by its serving count. Cooked weight and evaporation are not measured. Extra salt, oil and garnishes are excluded unless listed.

sipo-egg.name: Sipo Egg
sipo-egg.notes: Boil and peel the quail eggs. Saute aromatics and vegetables, simmer in water until tender, then add milk and eggs over gentle heat. Adaptation: one measured cup of evaporated milk replaces the source cup of cream. Quantities are measured inputs for the listed batch, divided by its serving count. Cooked weight and evaporation are not measured. Extra salt, oil and garnishes are excluded unless listed.

pesang-isda.name: Pesang Isda
pesang-isda.notes: Simmer aromatics in water, poach fish gently, then add pechay stems followed by leaves. Adaptations: snapper is the selected fleshy fish; optional green-onion garnish omitted. Counted produce uses the documented USDA reference size. Quantities are ingredient inputs for the listed batch, divided by its serving count. Cooked weight and evaporation are not measured. Extra salt, oil and garnishes are excluded unless listed; record measured additions when used.

cardillong-isda.name: Cardillong Isda
cardillong-isda.notes: Coat fish lightly with flour and pan-cook in the listed oil. Cook onions and tomatoes with water, then simmer with fish and egg whites until cooked. Uses three tomatoes from the source range; pepper and green-onion garnish omitted. Counted produce uses the documented USDA reference size. Quantities are ingredient inputs for the listed batch, divided by its serving count. Cooked weight and evaporation are not measured. Extra salt, oil and garnishes are excluded unless listed; record measured additions when used.

tinolang-manok.name: Tinolang Manok
tinolang-manok.notes: Saute chicken and aromatics, simmer in water, then cook sayote and add malunggay near the end. Uses the Hawaii Nutrition Center recipe's malunggay and permitted breast and chayote alternatives. Two cups of malunggay are 42 g using the USDA chopped-leaf measure; ginger uses a measured amount. Quantities are measured inputs for the listed batch, divided by its serving count. Cooked weight and evaporation are not measured. Extra salt, oil and garnishes are excluded unless listed.

lugaw.name: Lugaw
lugaw.notes: Simmer rice and ginger in water until the grains soften and the porridge thickens. Adaptation: this is the source porridge component without its separate fried-tofu accompaniment; ginger uses a measured amount. Counted produce uses the documented USDA reference size. Quantities are ingredient inputs for the listed batch, divided by its serving count. Cooked weight and evaporation are not measured. Extra salt, oil and garnishes are excluded unless listed; record measured additions when used.

lugaw-na-may-itlog.name: Lugaw na may Itlog
lugaw-na-may-itlog.notes: Prepare the source porridge component and add one measured hard-boiled egg per portion. This egg addition is an explicit adaptation; no swallowing-texture claim is made. Counted produce uses the documented USDA reference size. Quantities are ingredient inputs for the listed batch, divided by its serving count. Cooked weight and evaporation are not measured. Extra salt, oil and garnishes are excluded unless listed; record measured additions when used.

arroz-caldo.name: Arroz Caldo
arroz-caldo.notes: Saute aromatics and chicken, add rice and water, then simmer until chicken and rice are cooked. Divide the eggs among portions. Adaptations: the lower three-pound source amount is boneless breast; bouillon and separate fried-garlic garnish omitted. Counted produce uses the documented USDA reference size. Quantities are ingredient inputs for the listed batch, divided by its serving count. Cooked weight and evaporation are not measured. Extra salt, oil and garnishes are excluded unless listed; record measured additions when used.

champorado.name: Champorado
champorado.notes: Simmer glutinous rice in water, stir in chocolate and sugar, and serve with the measured milk. Adaptation: 15 g unsweetened cocoa is the defined replacement for source tablea; it is not asserted equivalent in weight or sweetness. Counted produce uses the documented USDA reference size. Quantities are ingredient inputs for the listed batch, divided by its serving count. Cooked weight and evaporation are not measured. Extra salt, oil and garnishes are excluded unless listed; record measured additions when used.

ginisang-monggo.name: Ginisang Monggo
ginisang-monggo.notes: Simmer monggo in water until tender. Saute aromatics and tomato, combine with the beans and liquid, then add malunggay and fish sauce. Adaptations: 42 g malunggay replaces the source spinach; chicharon is omitted. Quantities are measured inputs for the listed batch, divided by its serving count. Cooked weight and evaporation are not measured. Extra salt, oil and garnishes are excluded unless listed.
aliases: Mongo Guisado with Rice (Mung Bean Stew)

ginisang-monggo-sa-sardinas.name: Ginisang Monggo sa Sardinas
ginisang-monggo-sa-sardinas.notes: Simmer monggo in water until tender. Saute aromatics and tomato, combine with the beans and liquid, then add malunggay and fish sauce. Adaptations: 42 g malunggay replaces the source spinach; chicharon is omitted. Add the listed weighed canned sardines. Quantities are measured inputs for the listed batch, divided by its serving count. Cooked weight and evaporation are not measured. Extra salt, oil and garnishes are excluded unless listed.

ginisang-sayote.name: Ginisang Sayote
ginisang-sayote.notes: Cook the beaten eggs separately, saute aromatics and sayote until tender, then combine. Adaptation: seasoning powder and unquantified pepper omitted. Counted produce uses the documented USDA reference size. Quantities are ingredient inputs for the listed batch, divided by its serving count. Cooked weight and evaporation are not measured. Extra salt, oil and garnishes are excluded unless listed; record measured additions when used.

pinakbet.name: Pinakbet
pinakbet.notes: Saute pork and aromatics with bagoong, add water, then cook vegetables in stages until tender. Adaptations: measured butternut squash replaces the unweighed source squash; 120 g sitaw replaces the unweighed bean bunch. The named bagoong product supplies its label nutrients. No extra salt. Quantities are measured inputs for the listed batch, divided by its serving count. Cooked weight and evaporation are not measured. Extra salt, oil and garnishes are excluded unless listed.

chopsuey.name: Chopsuey
chopsuey.notes: Parboil vegetables, retain the listed water for the sauce, then stir-fry meat and aromatics. Add vegetables, oyster sauce, cooked quail eggs and cornstarch slurry. Adaptations: breast replaces thigh, broccoli uses half a USDA bunch and cauliflower half a medium head; baby corn omitted. Counted produce uses the documented USDA reference size. Quantities are ingredient inputs for the listed batch, divided by its serving count. Cooked weight and evaporation are not measured. Extra salt, oil and garnishes are excluded unless listed; record measured additions when used.

lumpiang-sariwa.name: Lumpiang Sariwa
lumpiang-sariwa.notes: Cook four crepe wrappers from flour, salt, sugar, egg and milk. Blanch the weighed filling vegetables. Simmer the peanut sauce, fill wrappers with vegetables and lettuce, and divide the sauce among four portions. Adaptations: jicama replaces ubod; low-fat milk and unsalted peanut butter replace the source branded dairy and spread. All listed sauce is counted. Counted produce uses the documented USDA reference size. Quantities are ingredient inputs for the listed batch, divided by its serving count. Cooked weight and evaporation are not measured. Extra salt, oil and garnishes are excluded unless listed; record measured additions when used.

sinangag.name: Sinangag
sinangag.notes: Cook garlic in oil, add cooked rice, separate the grains and stir-fry until heated through; season with the measured salt. Adaptation: six measured cloves replace the unweighed garlic head. Counted produce uses the documented USDA reference size. Quantities are ingredient inputs for the listed batch, divided by its serving count. Cooked weight and evaporation are not measured. Extra salt, oil and garnishes are excluded unless listed; record measured additions when used.

oatmeal-na-may-saging.notes: Cook measured oats in water and add the weighed banana. This is a defined ingredient-input portion. Counted produce uses the documented USDA reference size. tinapay-at-itlog.notes: Serve the weighed white bread with one measured hard-boiled egg. White bread is the actual nutrient record; it is not presented as a verified pandesal record. references.Lugaw with Egg (Soft Diet): Rice porridge with hard-boiled egg. Suitable for post-op, soft diet, and swallowing difficulty orders.
references.Lugaw with Chicken (Soft Diet): Rice porridge with shredded chicken breast. High-protein soft diet option.
references.Boiled Chicken Breast: Unseasoned boiled chicken breast. Low sodium, high protein. Suitable for most therapeutic diets.
references.Chicken Breast with Pechay: Boiled chicken breast with cooked pechay. Pair with a separately selected carbohydrate only when prescribed.
references.Steamed Tilapia: Lean white fish. Low sodium, good phosphate source. Suitable for most diets except CKD (monitor phosphate).
references.Steamed Milkfish (Bangus): Steamed milkfish. Rich in omega-3. Avoid in fish allergy patients.
references.Drained Sardines: Canned sardines in water (drained). Cost-effective protein. Note: moderate sodium.
references.Hard-Boiled Egg: One plain hard-boiled egg. Add a separately measured carbohydrate only when prescribed.
references.Tokwa with Kangkong: Firm tofu with water spinach. Plant-based protein. Contains soy — avoid for soybean allergy.
references.Plain Ginisang Monggo: Plain cooked mung beans. High fiber; add a separately measured carbohydrate only when prescribed.
references.Ampalaya with Tokwa: Bitter melon with firm tofu. High-fiber Filipino dish; add a separately measured carbohydrate only when prescribed.
references.Oatmeal with Banana: Plain oatmeal with banana. No added sugar. Suitable for DM breakfast — monitor potassium if renal diet.
references.Sweet Potato with Chicken: Baked sweet potato with boiled chicken breast. Low GI carbohydrate alternative.
references.Mixed Vegetable Plate: Boiled mixed vegetables. Low calorie, high fiber side dish suitable for all therapeutic diets.
references.Banana Snack: One banana. Quick, potassium-rich snack — avoid in high-K and renal-restricted diets.
references.Crackers and Milk Snack: Wheat crackers with low-fat milk. Between-meal nourishment. Contains wheat and milk.
references.Papaya Snack: Fresh papaya. Rich in vitamin C, fiber. Suitable for most diets.
references.Roasted Pork Loin: Plain roasted pork loin. Moderate fat. Add a separately measured carbohydrate only when prescribed.
references.Champorado (Chocolate Rice Porridge): Filipino chocolate rice porridge made with glutinous rice and cocoa. Very carb-heavy, low protein. Good for weight gain and high-energy needs.
references.Sinangag (Garlic Fried Rice): Filipino garlic fried rice. Mostly carbohydrates. Common Filipino breakfast staple. Low sodium version without soy sauce.
references.Arroz Caldo (Chicken Rice Soup): Filipino chicken congee with ginger. Balanced protein and carbs. Excellent for sick patients and soft diet.
references.Plain Oatmeal with Brown Sugar: Plain cooked oatmeal lightly sweetened. High fiber, low protein. Suitable for diabetic and cardiac diets (reduce or omit sugar for diabetic patients).
references.Pandesal with Egg: Filipino bread roll with boiled egg. Standard Filipino breakfast. Contains wheat.
references.Fresh Mango Serving: Fresh ripe Philippine mango. Naturally sweet, rich in vitamin C and A. Monitor potassium in renal diets.
references.Fresh Watermelon Snack: Fresh watermelon. Very low calorie, hydrating. Good for general diet. Limit in dialysis/fluid restriction.
references.Papaya with Calamansi: Fresh papaya with calamansi squeeze. Rich in vitamin C, fiber, and beta-carotene. Suitable for all diets.
references.Guava Snack: Fresh guava. Very high in vitamin C. High fiber. Low calorie. Suitable for diabetic and weight loss diets.
references.Boiled Corn (Mais): Plain boiled corn on the cob or kernels. Filipino street food staple. Good carbohydrate source, moderate fiber.
references.Boiled Kamote (Sweet Potato): Plain boiled sweet potato. Low GI, high in beta-carotene and fiber. Excellent for diabetic and weight management diets.
references.Pineapple Snack: Fresh pineapple. Contains bromelain, good for digestion. Monitor potassium in renal diet.
references.Jackfruit (Langka) Snack: Fresh jackfruit. Naturally sweet, high fiber, moderate carbohydrates. Rich in B vitamins.
references.Pinakbet (Hospital Version): Mixed vegetable stew without bagoong (shrimp paste) for low-sodium hospital version. Suitable for cardiac and hypertension diets.
references.Chopsuey: Chinese-Filipino mixed vegetable stir-fry, lightly seasoned. Serve any prescribed carbohydrate separately.
references.Bulanglang (Vegetable Soup): Tagalog-Visayan mixed vegetable soup. Very low calorie, high micronutrients. Suitable for all diets.
references.Ginisang Sayote (Sautéed Chayote): Lightly sautéed chayote with garlic and onion. Low calorie, good for renal diet (low potassium), suitable as side dish.
references.Ensaladang Talong (Eggplant Salad): Roasted eggplant salad with tomato and onion. Low calorie Filipino salad. Good for cardiac and weight loss diets.
references.Ampalaya Salad with Tomato: Bitter melon salad with tomato. Low calorie, high fiber. Traditional diabetes management food in Filipino culture.
references.Mongo Guisado (Mung Bean Stew): Sautéed mung bean stew with kangkong and garlic. High fiber, moderate protein, very Filipino. Good for diabetic and cardiac diets.
references.Paksiw na Bangus: Milkfish braised in vinegar and spices. Filipino fish dish. Moderate sodium from vinegar braising. Monitor in strict low-sodium diets.
references.Sinigang na Bangus (Simplified): Milkfish in tamarind-style sour broth with vegetables. Hospital version without commercial sinigang mix (lower sodium). High in omega-3.
references.Tinolang Manok (Chicken Ginger Soup): Filipino chicken soup with ginger, chayote, and malunggay. Balanced, low fat. Suitable for most therapeutic diets.
references.Ginisang Monggo with Sardines: Mung bean soup with canned sardines and kangkong. Budget-friendly, high fiber, good omega-3.
references.Tilapia Sinigang (Simplified): Tilapia in light sour broth with vegetables. Low fat, lean protein. Hospital version without commercial sinigang mix.
references.Mackerel Adobo Flakes: Mackerel flaked in light adobo sauce with garlic. Good omega-3, moderate protein. Suitable for most diets.
references.Boiled Cassava (Kamoteng Kahoy): Plain boiled cassava. Very high carbohydrate, low protein. Traditional Filipino root crop snack. Good for weight gain diets.
references.Ginataan (Coconut Fruit Dessert): Filipino dessert with sweet potato and banana in coconut milk. High energy, moderate fat. Good for weight gain and high-energy needs.
references.Lugaw (Plain Rice Porridge): Plain rice porridge without any topping. Very low protein, mostly carbohydrates. Suitable for strict renal diets, post-op, and low-residue orders.
